findings.reasoning: Filename contains only database and UTC timestamp to seconds; two authorized same-directory requests in same second choose same path, regardless distinct row GUID. BACKUP WITH FORMAT permits media replacement. Simultaneous SQL calls can instead fail; no particular concurrency outcome asserted. Sequential short backups can collide too. Retention protects newest valid record ID but does not deduplicate underlying paths, so duplicate records undermine file identity protection.
findings.counterevidence: Destination requires authorized backup actor/configured directory, SQL permissions and actual engine file access. COPY_ONLY preserves external backup-chain semantics; values parameterized and database identifier validated. No anonymous SQL injection claim.
findings.required_tests: Pure fixed-clock destination uniqueness and record/path retention model; physical SQL reproduction only in approved disposable instance.

findings.reasoning: Pending-count snapshot85-86 is not exclusive admission barrier. Checkout stages Pending and Complete in same scoped transaction before save/commit; another context cannot treat that as reliable census of running requests. After safety backup returns119 and before SINGLE_USER153, new financial request may commit and acknowledge. Restore replaces it, while earlier safety backup need not contain it. Later SQL exclusive access occurs too late to close this gap.
findings.counterevidence: Restore is intentionally destructive and strongly gated: permission/approval, literal confirmation, reason, file existence and mandatory successful safety backup. Planned rollback of post-backup history is inherent; finding concerns acknowledged work accepted during purported safe maintenance window. SINGLE_USER excludes/rolls back remaining connections only when reached. No actual lost transaction observed.
findings.required_tests: Pure admission/drain coordinator model; approved dedicated disposable SQL instance with injected checkpoints and last-acknowledged record recovery assertion.

findings.counterevidence: Same-request replay and unique OpenRequestId constrain duplicate identical commands. Pure Open/Reopen rules reject already-visible other active day. These do not enforce atomic singleton across concurrent distinct requests.
